absent: First-chunk creation, unit-to-CPU mapping, and runtime per-CPU allocation and free behavior beyond constants and descriptors.
Timing and context for percpu_ref release and confirm-switch callbacks and for transitions between atomic and per-CPU modes.
Sharded counter spill thresholds, batch tuning, and CPU hotplug handling.
Shrinker registration, scan scheduling, deferred-count aggregation, and debug interface behavior.
Architecture-specific per-CPU access primitives and enabled preemption-check behavior.
Interaction of module reservation with dynamic reserve exhaustion and out-of-memory handling.

findings.text: Declaration and definition helpers place per-CPU objects into read-mostly and decrypted sections, while export helpers either publish a per-CPU symbol for loadable modules or expand to nothing when module export is unavailable.

Per-CPU pointer helpers validate the per-CPU qualification of an address, convert it to a plain kernel address, and apply a CPU offset with relocation hiding; reduced configurations resolve both raw and current-CPU pointers to CPU zero.

Current-CPU accessors disable preemption before resolving the local instance and their counterparts re-enable preemption afterward, keeping the caller on one CPU across the pair; forms exist for named variables and for explicit pointers.
An indexed accessor yields the instance of a per-CPU variable that belongs to an explicitly supplied CPU number.

Size dispatch helpers verify per-CPU qualification and select among one, two, four and eight byte implementations based on object size, invoking a bad-size handler for other sizes; variants cover value return, value return with extra arguments, boolean return, and no return.

Raw per-CPU primitives provide read, write, additive update, bit mask updates, additive update with result, exchange, and compare-exchange behavior without preemption checking, with subtract and step adjustments expressed through addition.

Double-underscore current-CPU primitives run a preemption-state check that names the requested operation and then delegate to the matching raw primitive, with derived arithmetic again reusing addition.

Unprefixed current-CPU primitives dispatch by object size to their own sized implementations for read, write, mask updates, additive update with result, exchange, and compare-exchange, with subtract and step variants derived from addition.

Reference state splits into a compact handle with a tagged pointer plus a side pointer, and a side record with a shared atomic count, release and switch-confirm callbacks, single-bit force-atomic and allow-reinit flags, an RCU head, and a back link to the handle.
Two low pointer bits encode atomic versus per-CPU accounting and live versus dead condition, with a combined value for the both-set case and a recorded width for the flag field.

Start-up options select beginning locked in atomic mode, beginning dead with zero count until revived, or allowing later transition from atomic to per-CPU operation; the dead start implies the other behaviors and the atomic start implies reinit permission.

A kill helper terminates liveness through a confirm-capable path without supplying a confirmation callback, while live-acquisition helpers only succeed while the target remains live, with a plain wrapper bracketing the RCU-protected attempt with lock acquisition and release.

The RCU-protected live attempt expects an active RCU read section and otherwise warns; in per-CPU mode it credits the current CPU shard, otherwise it conditionally credits the shared count unless the dead mark is present, reporting whether acquisition succeeded.
Minimum per-CPU allocation granularity uses shift two for size four, and bitmap blocks span one page with bit capacity derived from block size shifted by that granularity.
Smallest per-CPU unit is page-aligned thirty-two kibibytes, and module reservation is eight kibibytes when enabled and zero otherwise.
Dynamic chunk shift is thirteen, twelve, or ten by configuration; early dynamic area spans twenty chunks and dynamic reserve spans twenty-eight or twenty chunks by configuration.

First-chunk metadata records per-group unit counts, base offsets, and CPU maps with empty slots marked, plus a descriptor with static, reserved, dynamic, unit, atom, and total sizes, internal size, group count, and group array, and a selector for automatic, embed, or page strategy with a count sentinel.

Per-CPU allocation helpers forward size, alignment, reservation choice, and allocation flags to a shared non-profiling allocator wrapped with hooks, with typed conveniences deriving size and alignment from the requested type.
The scalable counter has two shapes: a sharded form with a raw spinlock, central total, optional hotplug list node, and per-CPU shards, and a compact form holding only the central total.

Sharded counters serialize central updates with their embedded raw spinlock, the compact limited update masks interrupts around its check and commit, and the empty destroy paths require no synchronization.

Counter management offers multi-instance initialization with a lock identity, single-instance convenience, single and multi destroy, initialization checks, fast central read versus exact summation, explicit assignment, and a no-effect sync in compact mode.

Comparison reports ordering against a threshold, limited addition commits only when the result stays on the allowed side of a bound and signals success, local addition uses an unbounded batch or plain addition, and step and subtract helpers reuse addition.
Local-only counter batching uses the largest representable integer, effectively deferring central aggregation.
Deferred shrinker accounting groups per-unit deferred counts with a presence bitmap, topped by an RCU-protected descriptor holding maximum map size and a flexible array of unit pointers.
Reclaim requests carry allocation flags, target node, requested scan count, completed scan count, and target memory group; counts refresh before each call and the callee tracks its own progress.

A shrinker bundles count and scan callbacks, a reclaim batch where zero selects a default, a recreation-cost estimate, flag bits, a reference count with completion and RCU head, private data, a global list node, optional control-group and debug records, and per-node deferred counts.
Shrinker bitmap width equals machine word width, registration and allocation occupy the first two flag bits, default recreation cost is two, and stop and empty use the top two unsigned long values.

Registered shrinkers start with one reference that permits lookup-based acquisition, drop that initial reference at unregister time, and retire asynchronously through RCU once the count reaches zero, with completion allowing waiters to observe termination.
Each routed header defines a once-only inclusion guard macro that marks the header as already processed.
First-chunk placement can be customized through callbacks that map a CPU to a node and that report distance between two CPUs.
